newsitem.title: USA: NYC's Giuliani blocks subway workfare plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC's Giuliani blocks subway workfare plan - paper.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Guiliani has blocked transit officials from putting in place a plan to have welfare recipients clean the subway system, the New York Times reported Wednesday.

As a result, Metropolitan Transportation Authority will have to hire about 100 full-time workers instead. In recent months, the Authority has seen about 170 subway cleaners retire, and under a pact reached with the union, it had expected to get welfare recipients from the city to do their jobs, the paper explained.

However, the Guiliani Administration has opposed the plan since it was announced last September, saying welfare recipients should be used for temporary jobs, like cleaning parks and picking up trash, performing work that would not replace the tasks done by salaried workers, the paper said.
The Authority, realizing the city would not provide the welfare recipients, last Friday began taking applications for the 170 positions, it added.
